summary: Specifies SHA-224, a 224-bit one-way hash function. It is based on SHA-256 but starts from a different initial value and truncates the result to 224 bits, giving a hash size that matches the key strength of some other algorithms.

eli5.summary: A hash turns any file into a short fingerprint. This one makes a medium-sized fingerprint by shortening a bigger one.

subtitle: SHA-224: SHA-256 with a different starting value and the output cut to 224 bits.

tldr.problem: NIST key-management guidance discusses security levels of 80, 112, 128, 192 and 256 bits, and one-way hash functions existed for all of them except 112 bits.
tldr.mechanism: SHA-224 computes SHA-256 with a different set of eight initial 32-bit values and then keeps only the first seven 32-bit words of the result.
tldr.outcome: It gives a 224-bit digest providing 112 bits of security, the generally accepted strength of Triple-DES, and the RFC also publishes its test vectors and object identifier.

today: RFC 3874 is an Informational RFC from September 2004 and has not been obsoleted or updated. It remains the RFC that specifies SHA-224 and publishes its object identifier.

sections.title: Why SHA-224 Exists
sections.content:
The RFC makes the SHA-224 one-way hash function, announced by NIST in a FIPS 180-2 Change Notice on February 28, 2004, available to the Internet community. One-way hash functions are also known as message digests. SHA-224 is based on SHA-256.

NIST's key management guidance discusses five security levels: 80, 112, 128, 192 and 256 bits. Hash functions were available for all but one; SHA-224 fills the gap by providing 112 bits of security, the generally accepted strength of Triple-DES.
sections.eli5: There were fingerprint machines for most sizes except one. SHA-224 is the missing size.

sections.title: How SHA-224 Is Computed
sections.content:
SHA-224 can hash a message whose length is less than 2^64 bits. It is defined exactly like SHA-256, which uses a message schedule of sixty-four 32-bit words and eight 32-bit working variables and produces a hash of eight 32-bit words, with two exceptions.

First, the initial hash value H is a different set of eight 32-bit words. Second, only the first seven 32-bit words of the SHA-256 result are used, H_0 through H_6 joined together, and the last word is discarded. That gives 224 bits.
sections.eli5: Run the bigger fingerprint machine from a different starting point, then tear off the last piece of its answer.

sections.title: Usage Guidance
sections.content:
Computing SHA-224 takes roughly the same effort as SHA-256. The different initial value ensures that a truncated SHA-256 digest cannot be mistaken for a SHA-224 digest of the same data. The digest is 4 octets smaller, which matters in environments sensitive to every octet transmitted.

The guidance is: when choosing a suite of algorithms that all offer 112 bits of security, SHA-224 is an appropriate hash. When terseness is not a selection criterion, SHA-256 is the preferred alternative.
sections.eli5: If you need the shorter fingerprint, use SHA-224. If size does not matter, the longer one is better.

sections.title: Test Vectors and Object Identifier
sections.content:
Three test vectors let implementers check their code. Hashing the 24-bit string "abc" gives 23097d22 3405d822 8642a477 bda255b3 2aadbce4 bda0b3f7 e36c9da7. The other two inputs are a 448-bit string beginning "abcdbcdecdef" and 1,000,000 repetitions of the character "a".

NIST has assigned an ASN.1 object identifier for SHA-224, id-sha224, and protocols that name hash functions by identifier, such as CMS (RFC 3852), MUST use it when they use SHA-224.
sections.eli5: The test vectors are answers in the back of the book, so you can check your homework. The object identifier is the official name tag for SHA-224.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Hash functions are typically used with signature algorithms, keyed-hash message authentication codes, or random value generation. Such algorithms may require a hash with the same number of bits of security as themselves; SHA-224 is intended to provide 112 bits.

The author makes no independent assertion of the security of the function. However, as long as SHA-256 provides the expected security, SHA-224 will also provide its expected level.
sections.eli5: SHA-224 is only as strong as the bigger machine it is built from.
